knee_flex.source: PureGym 45-degree leg press: press up without locking the knees (15 degrees); lower until the thighs reach roughly 90 degrees, keeping the glutes and lower back stationary against the pad

hip_flex.source: 45-degree leg press guides: the hips track with the knees through the same range, since the platform moves the legs as a unit; the limit is the same 90-degree depth before the lower back rounds

torso_lean.source: ISSA leg press guide: "When the buttocks and lower back come up off the pad, this causes excessive rounding in the lumbar spine"; keep "your glutes and back against the pad and secured in position"

muscles.peakSource: no source gives a within-rep EMG timing for the leg press; the deepest controlled position, just before the drive back up, is the greatest mechanical disadvantage, so this is a reasoned placement, not a specific citation

mistake.name: Lock and round

tells.text: The knees slam to a hard lockout at the top of the press.
The hips curl and the lower back rounds off the pad at the bottom.

mistake.source: GymPT: "Full extension is not the same as snapping the knees back. Hard lockout shifts tension away from the muscles"; ISSA: "When the buttocks and lower back come up off the pad, this causes excessive rounding in the lumbar spine and can lead to injury"

sources: Contact fact (bar/platform over mid-foot): PureGym — feet placed "shoulder-width apart on the footplate, with your toes pointed slightly outward"; a real-world description, not a numeric `machine.settings` value this research can cite
